target.statement: SVM Regression achieves R2 = 0.889 (RMSE = 0.326) for predicting mpg on the Motor Trend dataset
target.dataset: Motor Trend US magazine 1974 (mtcars, N=398 as claimed; actually 32 rows)

compute.basis: mtcars is bundled with scikit-learn/statsmodels; SVR on a tiny table trains in seconds, so the only cost is installing scikit-learn and writing the pipeline.

blockers: No code or configs released; pipeline (feature selection, scaling, 70/30 split with random_state=1, SVR hyperparameters) must be guessed
Paper claims N=398 but mtcars has 32 rows, so exact numbers may not be reproducible
Reported metrics (e.g., CV scores of 0 for SVM/RF, inconsistent class metrics) look unreliable
title: Fuel Consumption Prediction: A Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Paradigms
